   "Renewed AI jitters drove the Nasdaq down over 5% and the SOX down over 10% in the week to 16-Oct-26, the worst week for both since Liberation Day. The VIX rose 3.5pts to close just shy of 20 and reached about 22 intraday. BofA reads this as a positioning-driven hiccup on the fringes of the AI trade, not secular weakness in the core.",
   "Pain was concentrated in high beta, highly levered names such as CRWV and NBIS rather than the Mag8 megacaps. Initial triggers could have been frontier lab ARR slowdown concerns or a hotter-than-expected PPI.",
   "US equities are rotating rather than rupturing under stress. Defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) outperformed tech to a historic degree over 14-16 Oct, comparable to Dotcom-bubble periods, which BofA reads as a sign that wider panic remains subdued.",
   "The 16-Oct VIX spike looks like a mini-fragility event. The close-to-close VIX move was outsized relative to the muted SPX move given the recent low VIX-SPX beta. The VIX vs SPX 1m ATM vol spread widened, as in Feb 2018 and Aug 2024, driven by SPX downside tail vol.",
   "Short VIX gamma exposure was above the 96th percentile since 2014 ahead of Friday's event, so positioning-driven amplification likely played a role. VIX call hedge monetization and dealer re-hedging flows were both visible.",
   "Healthcare and staples now sit among the highest BofA Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI) readings in the market, as the Nasdaq, Nikkei and Kospi BRIs retreat. Their implied vols are still historically low versus XLK vol and are among the cheapest sector vols relative to trailing 1m realized vol.",
   "BofA recommends two near-term relative value trades to hedge a reversal of the anti-tech rotation: buy XLP puts funded by XLK puts, and buy XLV puts funded by XLK puts. Both trade at a small credit.",
   "For longer-horizon protection against AI-driven drawdowns, BofA keeps its preference for NDX max lookback puts contingent on lower 10y rates. Last week NDX fell 5.5% while 10y yields fell 16bps, which BofA says supports an equity-down, rates-down pattern like the 2000-01 Dotcom unwind.",
   "European credit spreads (iTraxx Main and Senior Financials) have widened toward YTD highs while equity vol stays subdued. BofA recommends a long SX7E Jun27 260 put versus short 5y Senior Fin CDS protection, sized at an 8.8x credit-to-equity notional from historical beta.",
   "The SX7E trade offers about 25x risk/reward in risk-off scenarios, and the CDS carry and roll (+81bp) more than funds the put premium if CDS is unchanged or normalizes. SX7E is only about 12% off its all-time high after a roughly 200% rally in 3 years.",
   "BofA GFSI rose from -0.01 on 9-Oct-26 to +0.09 on 16-Oct-26, the 57th percentile since 2000. Equities drove most of the increase, with S&P 500 and Nikkei skew the biggest stress gainers. Rates and credit stress edged higher, and FX and commodity stress edged lower. The GFSI Risk Allocator moved to neutral from a 7.3% overweight.",
   "The BRI for S&P 500 stocks shows 13 stocks above 0.8 versus 50-100 at the dotcom peak, and 2.8% of index weight versus 20-40% then. BofA calls froth localized. Highest S&P 500 BRI readings: MRNA, KO, RVTY, ZBRA.",
   "Among themes, the Brazil Election basket (0.90) and the US Cyber Security basket (0.83) show the highest BRI. Pharma had the largest one-week BRI jump among popular themes.",
   "Cross-asset hedging screen: FX puts, especially CADUSD, are the cheapest tail hedges. Aluminium puts and Gold calls screen well on a post-2021 basis. Equity hedges look expensive in any sample, with HSI and HSCEI puts better value than other equity hedges. US IG credit payers look expensive over the past 5 years.",
   "Credit spreads, particularly in high yield, have widened materially over the past month, and rates and equity vol have moved higher, while FX and commodity vol dipped modestly. BofA cites fiscal concerns, sticky inflation and higher-for-longer rates as the backdrop.",
   "BRI methodology: it combines returns, realized vol, momentum and fragility across short, medium and long horizons on a 0-1 scale. Readings above 0.8 are a rule of thumb for elevated bubble risk. BofA treats it as a 'watch out' tool for adding protection, not a sell signal, because 3m max upside after high readings is similar to that at low readings."

  "title": "BofA Securities Equity Client Flow Trends: Extreme outflows week",
  "type": "strategy",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "Clients sold US equities in the week of 10/12-10/16 (S&P 500 -1.9%), led by record single stock outflows of -$14.8bn, the 25th largest when normalized by S&P 500 market cap. Clients bought equity ETFs (+$2.8bn) after selling the prior week.",
   "All client groups sold US equities. Institutional clients led (3rd week of selling, 10th biggest selling week by this group since 2008). Retail sold after buying the prior 2 weeks. Hedge funds sold for the first time in 5 weeks.",

 {
  "source": "Bank of America",
  "title": "From AI To KO: BofA Says The Flight-To-Safety Has Become A Bubble Of Its Own",
  "type": "derivatives",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "BofA's Global Equity Volatility Insights note 'Defensives can bubble too' finds the highest US Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI) readings are now in healthcare and consumer staples, not semis.",
   "Last week the Nasdaq fell more than 5% and the SOX more than 10%, the worst week for both since April 2025. The SOX fell eight straight sessions, matching its longest losing streak since 2006.",
   "BofA calls the selloff a largely positioning-driven hiccup on the edges of the AI trade. CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) fell 20-25% on the week, far more than their betas implied, while Mag8 megacaps tracked their betas.",
   "The 5-day spread between S&P defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) and tech blew out to levels seen only during the dotcom bubble. BofA says US equities rotate sharply under stress rather than rupture.",
   "On Friday Oct 16 the VIX rose about 6 points intraday toward 22 and closed the week at 19.99, up from 14.84 a week earlier. The move exceeded the expected reaction to a roughly 1.5% S&P drop, in an index that had gone 53 sessions without a 1% decline until the prior Wednesday.",
   "BofA calls the VIX spike a positioning-driven 'mini-fragility event'. Tell 1: the VIX move was too large relative to the SPX decline, after weak VIX-SPX beta in recent weeks. Tell 2: the VIX vs SPX 1-month ATM vol spread widened as downside tail vol drove the VIX, as in Feb 2018 and Aug 2024.",
   "Dealer short gamma in the VIX complex (ETPs plus options) going into Friday was larger than at any point outside the top 4% of readings since 2014. Investors monetizing VIX call hedges dampened the spike while dealer re-hedging amplified it, and the amplifiers won.",
   "Bloomberg cites a BofA estimate that a 10-point shock in front-month VIX futures could force dealers to buy roughly 90% of a day's VIX futures volume to stay delta-neutral.",
   "BRI is a price-based 0-to-1 score built from returns, realized volatility, momentum and convexity. BofA uses 0.8 as its danger line: seven of eight historical bubbles peaked above it.",
   "US healthcare had the highest BRI among BofA's global indices, US sectors, commodities and crypto, near 0.8. Energy and staples were each about 0.67 and tech about 0.5. Nasdaq, Nikkei and Kospi BRIs retreated (chart-read, approximate).",
   "The 'US Pharma Hyperscalers' custom basket reads 0.75. US cybersecurity is at 0.83 and Brazil's election basket is highest at 0.90. Pharma had the biggest weekly jump in bubble risk among popular themes.",
   "The S&P 500 stocks with the highest BRI are Moderna (MRNA), Coca-Cola (KO), Revvity (RVTY) and Zebra (ZBRA). Amgen, Merck, Agilent, Thermo Fisher, Quest Diagnostics and Smucker are also in the top 25, and healthcare is about half the list.",
   "Positioning: Morgan Stanley's prime book showed hedge fund healthcare exposure in the 3rd percentile of the past year, and Goldman said funds de-grossed the sector four straight weeks. Privorotsky noted quality rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with an RSI of 83.",
   "BofA says the froth is localized. Only 13 S&P stocks have a BRI above 0.8, or 2.8% of index market cap, versus 50-100 stocks and 20-40% of market cap at the dotcom peak. A high BRI is a cue to buy protection, not a sell signal.",
   "BofA's trade view: XLP and XLV implied vols are about the 20th percentile versus XLK vol, cheap against their own realized vol, while XLK vol screens rich. Bloomberg says staples hedging costs fell more than any other sector last week.",
   "BofA recommends two relative-value put trades, both about 25-delta and for a small credit: XLP vs XLK, and XLV vs XLK. For those wary of naked XLK puts into earnings, FOMC and the midterms, it suggests XLK put spreads as the funding leg.",
   "Longer-dated hedge: NDX Sep27 max lookback puts contingent on 10Y rates falling. Last week's NDX -5.5% and 10Y -16bps supported BofA's view that an AI unwind resembles 2000-01, with equities and rates both down.",
   "Goldman's healthcare desk noted that Monday's TMT/AI bounce drove defensive underperformance, so the two sides of the rotation trade like a single toggle.",
   "ZeroHedge's own view: if last week was more than a hiccup, the AI financing squeeze (hyperscaler CDS at record wides) could hit defensives too, as in a true liquidation investors sell what they still own."

 {
  "source": "Zerohedge , summarizing HSBC and Goldman Sachs research",
  "title": "HSBC Destroys Goldman's CoreWeave Upgrade: \"The More It Invests, The More The Value Destruction\"; Sees Crash To $39",
  "type": "equity_research",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "HSBC (Abhishek Shukla) reiterated Reduce on CoreWeave with a $39 price target, 36.5% below Friday's close, one day after Goldman (Gabriela Borges) upgraded to Buy and cut its target from $139 to $106. The stock spiked to $66 on the upgrade, then gave back the entire gain.",
   "HSBC estimates CoreWeave earns an average 2026-30e ROIC of 8.9% including customer advances and negative working capital, below its cost of borrowing. HSBC's view is that more investment at this return profile adds more value destruction.",
   "HSBC uses the same 10% long-term pretax cost of debt as Goldman. Its WACC is 9.7%, below the 11.8% Goldman used in its illustrative contract math. The gap between $39 and $106 comes from revenue per MW, margins and interest costs.",
   "HSBC expects CoreWeave revenue of $12 million per MW per year in 2027, versus $17-18 million for hyperscalers. It attributes the gap to hyperscalers' short-term contracts, differentiated general-purpose cloud business and many small customers that buy the full stack.",
   "In HSBC's revenue-per-gigawatt math, CoreWeave earns about $12.1 billion per Nvidia-equivalent GW in 2027, versus $18.2 billion for Microsoft Azure and $21.7 billion for AWS. Only Oracle's cloud is comparable.",
   "HSBC argues neoclouds have weak balance sheets and depend on debt, so lenders require long-term contracts with large creditworthy customers that cover the full repayment period. This keeps them out of the short-term rental market.",
   "HSBC calculates CoreWeave's RPO covers 5.0 years of cloud revenue, versus 2.5 years at Amazon and 3.4 years at Google and Microsoft.",
   "Revenue is about 33% of gross assets ex-construction and leases. With GPUs depreciated over six years, depreciation is roughly 50% of revenue. Data center rent is 17-18% and power 5-6%, so over 70% of costs are fixed. HSBC's long-term non-GAAP operating margin is 15-16%, versus management's guidance of about 25%.",
   "HSBC has CoreWeave ROIC at 4.9% in 2027 and 5.0% in 2030 (high single digits including customer advances), versus AWS in the mid-to-high teens and Microsoft around 14%.",
   "Goldman cited short-term (3-6 month) contracts signing at $40 million per MW, about 4x the blended portfolio. HSBC agrees those deals happened but expects them not to last, because LLM provider revenue growth has moderated over the last three months.",
   "By the article's chart reading, LLM provider run-rate revenue rose from about $44 billion in March to about $105 billion in July, then to about $115 billion by September.",
   "HSBC notes SpaceX's May deals with Anthropic and Google, which could earn SpaceX $22-50 million per MW, are cancellable on three months' notice.",
   "Goldman's FICC desk (Mark Wilson) named two catalysts for last week's sharp price moves: CoreWeave co-founder McBee's comments on insurance capital availability, and a debate over frontier-lab business models and closed versus open model competition.",
   "Goldman argued CoreWeave's 13.5-15% unsecured yields are not representative of its cost of debt because the unsecured market has been closed to new issuance. HSBC reads yields of 14-15% as market concern over creditworthiness that limits financing of speculative or short-contract capacity.",
   "HSBC says consensus assumes a significant cut in CoreWeave's borrowing rate, which it considers increasingly unlikely. Its implied interest rate is 9.0% in 2029 versus 7.8% for the Street, a 112bps gap.",
   "Five-year CDS closed at a record 1,117bps last Wednesday. The 2031 bonds yield just over 15%, off a 16%+ peak last week.",
   "HSBC is 9.6% below consensus on 2030 revenue. Its 2030 non-GAAP operating profit of $11.2 billion is 46% below consensus, and its 2028-2030 EPS estimates are 54-71% below consensus.",
   "Goldman raised its 2028 EPS to $3.36, 3.5x HSBC's $0.96. Goldman's base case has FCF turning positive in 2030, while HSBC has FCF at -$22.9 billion in 2027 and -$5.9 billion in 2030, with net debt rising from $17.5 billion at end-2025 to $92.3 billion by 2030.",
   "HSBC expects CoreWeave to stay loss-making through 2029 if share-based compensation is treated as an expense.",
   "CoreWeave trades at 14.7x 2030e EV/non-GAAP EBIT after SBC versus 7-11x for hyperscalers, and at 0.78x EV/RPO versus 0.34x for Oracle. HSBC calls the premium unsustainable.",
   "Street targets range widely against a premarket price of about $58.6: HSBC $39 (33% downside), Goldman $106, BNP Paribas $117 (recently cut), Evercore ISI $150 and another at $169, implying 81% to 156% upside. JPMorgan said debt fears are overdone but expects negative FCF until 2030.",
   "HSBC has held Reduce since initiating in July 2025 with a $32 target when the stock was around $120. Its target has ranged between $32 and $44. Goldman's disclosures show a pending CoreWeave underwriting, a 1%+ holding and banking fees, while HSBC's disclosure checklist is blank.",
   "HSBC argues poor asset turnover reflects weak competitive dynamics, not short-term growth pains, so depreciation is unlikely to fall as a share of revenue.",
   "Neocloud peers are weak. Korea's Elice fell as much as 32% on its debut, and Gartner predicted over 80% of neoclouds will fold by 2030. Meta earnings tomorrow are the next test of customer capex."

  "title": "Cracks In The AI Boom",
  "type": "macro",

  "insights": [
   "The AI boom is currently driven by capex recycling rather than genuine end-user demand, raising concerns about the sustainability of the current revenue growth trajectory.",
   "Hyperscalers are pumping massive capital into the system, but returns on capital are falling short of the requirements needed to justify the projected $2.5-3.5 trillion annual hurdle rate by 2030.",
   "Leverage is increasing rapidly across the AI ecosystem, with significant debt exposure in unprofitable neoclouds, standalone model developers, and equipment providers.",
   "The tech hardware and chip sector is prone to bullwhip effects, with evidence of double and triple-ordering that could lead to a supply glut if demand slows.",
   "Accounting practices, including the 'depreciation cliff' and data center leasing structures, may be temporarily flattering balance sheets and masking underlying cash burn.",
   "External triggers, such as political backlash against AI or rate hikes, pose a greater threat to the sector than endogenous factors, as public sentiment remains skeptical."
  ],

   "UBS expects the FOMC to leave the fed funds target range unchanged at the October 27-28 meeting, after the September hike, with Chairman Warsh's message being 'we have more work to do'.",

   "UBS expects a 10-2 vote in October, with dissents from Beth Hammack and Lorie Logan. One or three dissents would not be a surprise. Kashkari may also dissent.",
   "The October skip reflects the proximity of the midterms and the nature of the inflation problem: 3% inflation not heading to 2% obviously or fast enough, not rising inflation or an overheating economy.",
   "UBS thinks Warsh leaned toward a sequence of three hikes. The strong September CPI likely reinforced the preference for three over two. Williams suggested only one more hike, while Waller's remarks pointed to a possible preference for two more.",
   "UBS expects the October statement to drop the sentence saying they raised rates and to add back 'The Committee will deliver price stability.' Warsh is expected to keep the press conference brief and lean on 'trend not the data point'.",
   "UBS projects 2026 core PCE inflation at 3.2% Q4/Q4, with little progress until 2.9% in the February 2027 data. Headline inflation is projected at 2.1% and core at 2.5% in Q2 2027 as energy base effects are lapped, with core stuck near 2.5% in H2 2027.",
   "UBS tracks Q3 real GDP at 3.6% and real PCE at 3.4% annualized, and Q4 GDP at 1.7% saar. Full-year 2026 growth is 2.5% Q4/Q4 and 2027 is 2.0%. Q3 equipment investment is about 25.2% annualized, with a -2.6 pp net export drag because much of the capital investment is imported.",
   "In 2027 fiscal policy flips from support to a mild headwind as tax refunds shrink, and higher rates weigh more on rate-sensitive sectors. AI investment is expected to stay very robust.",
   "Midterm risk: polling points to more Democratic control of Congress. A Democratic Senate could constrain the administration's Fed Board nominees. UBS expects as many as four governors could depart by early 2028, adding uncertainty about the FOMC's reaction function.",

   "Headline CPI rose 0.65% m/m and 3.74% y/y, up from 3.40% and versus 2.41% in February before the Iran conflict. Headline is below the 4.25% May peak.",

   "Takeaway 5: modular designs are becoming critical to scaling data center build-outs because systems can be manufactured and tested off-site, then installed and commissioned faster.",
   "Eaton: moving AC/DC conversion outside the compute rack changes the distribution and protection equipment needed. Eaton illustrated 125A circuits carrying about 100kW each at 800V.    "Eaton: DC current does not fall to zero periodically like AC, so fault interruption is harder, and batteries and capacitors can keep feeding a fault.    "A joint ABB/Eaton session stressed common voltage ranges, grounding practices, connectors and controls so equipment from different suppliers works together.",

   "BNY expects the Fed to present a firm stance on price stability, giving its message a hawkish skew.",
   "BNY is uncertain about the cadence of policy action. The committee leans toward removing accommodation, but Warsh proposed cutting the annual number of scheduled meetings and may prefer less frequent interventions.",

  "insights": [
   "UBS sales desk (Zain Nizami, 22-Oct-2026) argues the balance of risk is shifting from holding defensive exposure toward selectively buying weakness. Asia looks technically washed out while parts of Europe look overbought.",

   "The cross-asset backdrop is still elevated oil, wider OAT-Bund spreads and higher sovereign yields. Yields are now easing somewhat amid a flight to safety. Political and geopolitical headlines have accelerated these moves.",
   "Some correlations are re-emerging. Relative-value relationships, particularly Semis versus Software, are approaching extreme levels.",
   "The Hang Seng registered a 95% down day and Hong Kong absorbed most of the selling, though weakness was broad. KOSPI had 627 decliners against 152 advancers.",

   "Goldman's 25-route freight index shows the global average crude freight rate rose from about $3/bbl a year ago to above $20/bbl. Middle Eastern routes are above $35/bbl. The rate is seven times higher than a year ago.",

   "Goldman's baseline has Brent falling to $90/bbl by year-end and averaging $80/bbl in 2027. Even so, continued ship-to-ship transfers would be needed without reliable freedom of navigation through Hormuz. The US blockade is unlikely to be lifted without a peace deal.",

   "Nokia is shifting to 12-18 months of forward visibility for customers, compared to the 6-month or 'hand-to-mouth' cycle seen 18 months ago.",

 {
  "source": "JPMorgan",
  "title": "Flows & Liquidity: Bottoming out?",
  "type": "strategy",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "JPM's overall equity positioning metric is significantly lower than the mid-September peak. Some near-term headwinds from last week remain, but positioning adjustments could start to limit downside.",
   "Funding concerns around neoclouds (AI compute rental providers) took center stage over the past week. Credit research expects publicly listed neoclouds to shift toward equity financing and project-specific debt as high yield funding costs rise.",
   "Equity research notes that a higher cost of capital could limit return headroom for neoclouds, but strong compute demand may allow some cost pass-through to customers (CoreWeave note, Oct 16).",
   "JPM does not expect the AI capex cycle to be derailed even if the neocloud funding model becomes unviable. Publicly listed neoclouds are a small segment: about $30bn of the roughly $2.2tr of tech operating cash flows and about $80bn of the roughly $1.8tr of tech capex projected for this year.",
   "Other tech companies with stronger balance sheets, such as hyperscalers, could absorb the neoclouds' AI infrastructure build-out.",
   "The tech sector as a whole runs a financing surplus of about $400bn in 2026 because cash flows exceed capex, so it does not need external financing in aggregate. A scenario with capex growing 25% a year and cash flows 20% a year to 2030 still leaves a slight surplus.",
   "Tech sector debt issuance is driven mainly by the wish to maintain buybacks while capex rises. If funding stress spreads, tech firms could postpone buybacks and use circular financing, with surplus firms such as chip makers funding deficit firms such as neoclouds.",

  "insights": [
   "Global public debt is rising sharply, with the IMF projecting it to reach 100% of GDP by 2029, a level not seen since the aftermath of World War II.",
   "Debt sustainability is primarily driven by the interest-growth differential (r-g), the primary balance, and the direction of debt, rather than the debt-to-GDP ratio alone.",
   "The 'r-g' differential has turned unfavorable for many nations, creating a snowball effect where interest costs grow faster than the economy unless offset by primary surpluses.",
   "France is under particular scrutiny due to a large primary deficit, rising debt, and political gridlock, with its risk premium reaching levels seen during the euro crisis.",
   "An acute debt crisis is not the baseline scenario, as long debt maturities and existing European backstops (ECB, ESM) provide a buffer against immediate panic.",
   "A slow-moving crisis is more likely, where rising interest costs crowd out investment and social spending, leading to political tension and market volatility.",
   "Political credibility is the key trigger for crises; governments that lose the ability to deliver on fiscal promises face higher risk premiums regardless of their debt ratios.",

 {
  "source": "Zero Hedge , summarizing Bernstein, Goldman Sachs and HSBC research on CoreWeave",
  "title": "CoreWe've Got Bills To Pay: Bernstein Sees $76 Billion Funding Hole At Imploding Neocloud",
  "type": "equity_research",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "Bernstein (Madison Rezaei, Underperform since initiation seven months ago) cut its CRWV price target to $51 from $74 and its target EV/EBIT multiple to 23.5x from 25.5x, citing cost of capital as CoreWeave moves to shorter-dated contracts.",
   "Bernstein estimates CRWV needs to raise $85B to fund its existing committed backlog, $9B of which is covered by existing facilities. That leaves about $76B of new money before any new contract is signed.",
   "Goldman's follow-up note (Gabriela Borges, Buy upgrade on Monday) puts the funding gap at about $23B. Bernstein's figure is more than three times larger.",
   "Bernstein says stopping new contract wins would not fix the funding need. Deployment obligations in existing contracts plus maintenance and replacement capex still have to be paid, so profitability would not improve immediately.",
   "Bernstein models about $46B of growth capex next year plus about $6B of maintenance capex, for $52.5B in 2027, above consensus. Even with no future backlog, 2027 capex is $43.5B. Its capex is well below the Street from 2028 on.",
   "Bernstein widens its 2026 and 2027 adjusted EPS losses and models adjusted losses through at least 2029.",
   "Goldman's $23B depends on assumptions. It assumes 80% DDTL debt financing, nets $10.6B of undrawn DDTL capacity and $10.4B of cash optionality, and assumes customers prepay 20% of contract value ($15.7B). Stretching GPU useful life to six years lowers it to $19.5B.",
   "The article challenges Goldman's inputs. CoreWeave's prepayment percentages have fallen over six months, and the $10.4B of cash optionality includes $2.2B of ATM share sales at $64 (above the current price). It also counts a revolver of which $1.2B of $2.5B is already drawn per Bernstein.",
   "Goldman's 4.2GW scenario ($38B) assumes $52.7B of customer prepayments. Without them, new debt needed is $84.5B at a 94% debt-to-loan ratio, above the 80% DDTL cap Goldman cites. Goldman's note gives no cost of capital and defers to a 10% new-debt cost in its upgrade note.",
   "Goldman's own model shows free cash burn of $28.2B in 2026, $28.2B in 2027 and $15.8B in 2028, with debt rising $26.7B, $26.6B and $20.0B. Long-term debt rises from $14.9B (end 2025) to $90.8B (2028), interest coverage is 0.3x in 2026 and 0.7x in 2027, and cash falls to $1.2B at end 2027.",
   "Goldman discloses it is a manager or co-manager of a pending CoreWeave underwriting, owns 1% or more of the stock, and expects to seek investment banking compensation within three months.",
   "CoreWeave has $42.1B of debt and a $3.3B annual interest bill, a blended 7.8% rate held down by $10.8B of 2-3% converts. Gross debt is 8.6x LTM adjusted EBITDA, 11.7x on total committed capacity and 7.4x next year's EBITDA.",
   "Most debt matures in 2030-2032 (about $31B), so Bernstein does not expect distress soon. DDTLs amortize, with principal repayments and covenant tests starting well before maturity: DDTL 5.0 repayments begin around Oct 22 (CoreWeave says November), the first 1.35x DSCR test is around Nov 30, DDTL 5.5 amortizes from January and the $8.5B DDTL 4.0 next July.",
   "Unsecured bonds yield around 15%. DDTL 5.5 (August) priced at SOFR+5.50%, the widest since the first DDTL in 2023, and Bernstein thinks later deals could price higher.",
   "Shorter enterprise contracts capture higher pricing per MW but are riskier to creditors and do not lower CoreWeave's cost of capital. Bernstein assigns a low, nonzero probability to CoreWeave building a differentiated enterprise business.",
   "Bernstein's best-case Meta contract (including the $21B expansion) gives an unlevered IRR of 9-12% (9% illustrative). The levered IRR is 32%, driven by leverage and a $2.3B residual value in year six. HSBC reached a similar conclusion with an 8.9% ROIC.",
   "Bernstein does not call CRWV a zero because of its large backlog, line of sight to powered shell delivery and contracts that are not underwater. It thinks Nvidia would intervene in a true downside, which raises the floor but does not necessarily re-energize the stock.",
   "Bernstein calls the damage semi-contained: if CoreWeave ceased to exist, colo contracts would be absorbed. The article argues CoreWeave is still the AI credit beta barometer and the tenant on seven of the 20 project-finance data center bonds in the junk market.",
   "Price action: after Goldman's Monday upgrade the stock spiked to $66 premarket and gave back the gain after the open. HSBC set a $39 target on Tuesday. The stock fell another 8% to $56.70, below its pre-upgrade level and the 52-week low."

   "Compute demand is significantly greater than supply, so the speed of the data center buildout determines who benefits and who is hurt.",
   "Winners from a slower buildout are assets tied to scarce physical capacity: operating data centers, hyperscalers with power, land and chips already secured, holders of powered land and grid access, long-lead equipment makers, and power producers with on-site generation.",
   "Operating data centers can raise rents and fill every megawatt because new competitors cannot arrive quickly.",
   "Powered land with secured power, interconnection and permits is described as the scarcest input and hardest to replicate, so its value rises in a delay.",
   "Long-lead equipment suppliers (transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling) keep long backlogs and pricing power, with transformer lead times of up to 26 months.",
   "Where the grid is the bottleneck, gas turbines, fuel cells and batteries become more valuable.",
   "Hyperscaler growth and earnings lose in a delay: revenue is capped by supply rather than demand, committed capex keeps accruing while capacity sits idle, and pricing power on existing capacity only partly offsets this.",
   "AI labs, startups and enterprise buyers face rationing, higher prices and slower model training and product launches, with smaller players crowded out first.",
   "Developers and construction-stage investors see cash flows start later while interest and carrying costs continue. Leveraged or pre-lease-dependent developers face covenant and refinancing stress.",
   "Equity investors in the AI trade are exposed to earnings revisions and multiple compression, because valuations assume on-time delivery.",
   "The broader economy loses: near-term GDP growth, which leans on AI investment, is lower, AI productivity gains arrive later, and households and businesses on the same grid may see higher electricity costs.",

   "Higher memory prices are spilling into consumer electronics (phones, computers, consoles), which have larger weights in global inflation baskets than memory cards.",
   "Increased power demand from data centers is boosting US core PCE by 0.1-0.2pp, but has minimal impact elsewhere (less than 5bp) currently."

  "title": "Novartis (NOVN.S): Takeaways from our Multiple Sclerosis KOL call following remibrutinib data presentation at MSToronto 2026",
  "type": "equity_research",

  "insights": [
   "Goldman Sachs maintains a Sell rating on Novartis, viewing the 12% YTD outperformance vs. EU Pharma as unjustified given mixed financial results and recent pipeline disappointments.",
   "KOL feedback on remibrutinib data presented at MSToronto 2026 suggests moderate efficacy, with ARR benefits of 31-35% and 6-month CDP-EDSS of 29.2% missing the bar expected by investors (>40% ARR benefit).",
   "KOLs view the BTKi class as having moderate efficacy, with Roche's fenebrutinib holding an efficacy edge while Novartis' remibrutinib is perceived to have a better safety profile.",
   "Novartis guided to $8bn+ peak sales for remibrutinib ($4bn+ in RMS, $4bn+ in CSU/CIndU), but Goldman Sachs remains skeptical, modeling $3bn in MS and $7.6bn total risk-adjusted sales.",
   "The current RMS treatment paradigm remains dominated by anti-CD20 antibodies (Ocrevus, Kesimpta, Briumvi) due to high efficacy, safety, and ease of administration, limiting near-term BTKi uptake to 5-10% of RMS patients.",

   "The main structural change in U.S. equity markets over 15 years is the growing weight of long-duration capital (Retail Investors, Retirement Assets, Foreign Investors) next to fast growth in short-duration trading capital (Systematic, Quantitative, Hedge Fund strategies).",
   "Long-duration capital increasingly drives market trends and short-duration capital increasingly drives volatility. Corrections have become more frequent and sharper, and recoveries faster and more persistent.",

  "insights": [
   "The 'crowding out' thesis, which suggests AI investment demand is mechanically driving up interest rates and squeezing other sectors, is largely flawed due to the flexible nature of the financial system.",
   "There is no statistical relationship between tech security issuance and yields, and AI-related debt is currently trading at a discount with widened spreads.",
   "A softer version of the thesis holds some merit: the AI boom acts as demand stimulus that is net inflationary, adding approximately 0.3% to CPI.",
   "The macro footprint of the AI buildout is smaller than commonly perceived, as much of the stimulus leaks out of the US economy into the rest of the world via tech imports.",
   "The AI boom has influenced Fed perceptions of r* by masking weakness in residential construction with gains in non-residential construction.",
   "The report posits a 'crowding in' scenario: when the AI boom eventually ends, the Fed will likely cut rates aggressively, which should facilitate a mild downturn rather than a 2008-style crash."

  "insights": [
   "JPM's economists expect the fed funds rate to go from 4.00% to 4.25% in December and then hold. The 10-year yield is around the ~5.00% near-term expectation, and the report cites a 5.24% 10-year in the utilities section.",
   "Equity strategy base case is a shallow hiking cycle, a reversal of last year's insurance cuts, which equities can absorb given the earnings anchor. A broader cycle of four to five hikes would likely cause more significant downside and is not the base case.",
   "Over the past year expectations moved from cuts to hikes. Long-dated Treasuries are down about 7% and forward P/E has compressed by about 3x, but equities are still up 12% YTD on earnings growth of 28% for 2026 and 22% for 2027.",
   "The US 30-year yield is about 5.35%, near 20-year highs. JPM attributes the back-end selloff to central bank repricing, sticky inflation from oil and trade shocks, rising fiscal deficits, and possible crowding out as foreign investors shift toward corporate debt (LTM $403B vs ~$397B for Treasuries).",
   "Roughly 80 years of data show an inverted U between the 10-year yield and S&P 500 multiples. With above-trend EPS growth (~15% y/y) yields can rise to ~5% before multiples de-rate. With consensus forward EPS growth above 20% and the S&P at ~18x 2027 EPS, JPM says equities could withstand a 10-year yield of ~5.5-6.0%.",
   "Primary risk named is further geopolitical escalation in the Middle East creating a more severe inflation and growth shock. Other risks are weaker earnings growth and an abrupt, volatile bond selloff.",
   "First-order effect on corporate interest expense should be gradual because debt is mostly fixed and long-dated. Financials' higher profitability and returns on ~$2.4T of cash offset it near term. Pressure concentrates in lower-income consumers, smaller companies, highly leveraged firms and capital-intensive industries outside the AI buildout.",
   "Sector leadership depends on curve shape. Bear steepeners have favored Cyclicals such as Energy and Financials, bear flatteners have favored Technology, and bond proxies and long-duration sectors ex-Technology (Utilities, Real Estate, Comm Services, Staples) are most exposed. Base case keeps JPM in Growth and Quality Growth with large caps over small caps. A broader hiking cycle would argue for rotation into Low Vol.",
   "JPM launched three thematic baskets: Beneficiaries of Higher Rates (JPRHIRTB), Beneficiaries of Lower Rates (JPRLORTB) and Agnostic Beneficiaries (JPRAGRTB). Performance lookback chart shows the baskets at 93.7, 69.7 and 97.1 rebased to 100 (labels not mapped to values in the text).",
   "Higher-rate beneficiaries are asset-sensitive banks, BDCs, insurers, payroll and HSA float earners, net-cash restaurants and media, integrated oils, auto-parts retailers, waste services, EDA software, custom silicon and process control.",
   "Large banks: higher rates are positive for NII through lagged deposit repricing, with a modest, manageable hit to capital from HTM and AFS marks.    "BDCs: ARCC is JPM's preferred way to play higher rates, followed by BXSL. Both trade near 1.0x NAV vs 0.60-0.70x for most peers and kept their dividends. Commercial mortgage REITs (ABR, KREF) face non-accrual and resolution drag.",

   "Handelsbanken argues that underlying inflation is set to resurge, based on leading indicators, after a period when many gauges showed progress toward the 2 percent target.",
   "Handelsbanken criticizes Warsh for three things: appearing unaware of leading indicator signals, saying he does not know whether strong supply- and demand-driven US growth is contributing to inflation, and being too relaxed about inflation expectations, which many measures show are high and rising.",
